Mindtwitch Interactive website, 2008

A 2008 portfolio site for interactive designer Michael Boucher, dressed in aged paper, rusted metal, torn edges, and stencil tabs.

Context

Smashing Magazine’s March 2008 article “The Secrets of Grunge Design” links mindtwitch.com among its examples. Smashing Magazine.

Observed

  • The page sits on a dark brown leather texture. The central column is made of stained, yellowed parchment with torn, curled edges.
  • A frayed cloth and paper strip at the top carries the “mindtwitch” wordmark with a red star and the tagline “CREATIVELY TWISTED”.
  • Navigation tabs are dark red with beige stencil capitals (“CREATIONS”, “EXPERIENCE”, “THE BLOG”).
  • A rusted metal band runs across the page below the tabs and again at the foot.
  • A photograph of a figure in a gas mask is mounted in a white frame held by strips of tape.
  • The heading “Creations” is a red brush script over a faded, larger copy of itself; body text is a plain serif list in black, blue, and red.

Why it belongs

The measurement finds only two families (Trebuchet MS and Georgia) and no pattern share, because every texture is a bitmap image (image share 1.0). This is typical of 2000s grunge web design: surfaces carry the style, and HTML type stays conventional.

Borrow

Tear the edges of a content panel with an image mask and let a faded, oversized copy of the heading sit behind the heading.
